name: Champion of the Impassioned Warrior
body:
Champions of the Impassioned Warrior are driven by an unwavering commitment to protect and defend their loved ones. They draw upon the fierce aspects of Ares’ wife, Aphrodite Areia, goddess of love and war. These warriors channel their intense emotions into battle prowess, fighting with unrivaled determination and unwavering loyalty.

Background: Most Champions of the Impassioned Warrior are drawn to Aphrodite’s warrior aspect at a young age. They join the temple for training and begin their careers as warriors serving and protecting their community. Many belong to a warrior society, such as Sparta or Argos.

Ancestries: Aphrodite Areia’s followers are usually human, though nymphs, elves, giant kin and gnomes are also found among the ranks of Impassioned Warriors.

Homeland: Most Impassioned Warriors are from Anatolia or Greece. A few are from Magna Graecia, Gaul, or North Africa. Rarely are these warriors found in other lands.

Role: Impassioned Warriors embody the fiery emotions and unwavering devotion of Aphrodite Areia. Their hearts burn with intensity, fueling their combat prowess and inspiring those around them. With their zealous determination, they lead the battlefield charge, unleashing their inner strength to protect and fight for their loved ones.

Religion: Impassioned Warriors are always devoted to Aphrodite Areia and her doctrine of fierce, emotionally driven war. This doesn’t preclude these champions from honoring or worshiping other deities, but it does mean they hold Aphrodite Areia above all others.

Alignment: Impassioned Warriors are loyal, but they also find power in the chaotic tides of emotion.

Aphrodite

Areia emphasizes the strength and might that stem from intense, maddening emotions such as love. For these reasons Champions of the Impassioned Warrior must be some form of chaotic alignment.

Adventures: Champions of the Impassioned Warrior are determined to ensure the safety and security of their loved ones. They will eagerly undertake any mission and achieve any objective necessary to protect their loved ones. As guardians, saviors, and avengers, they are well armed and trained for combat. Whether protecting a revered figure within their cult’s extended family, venturing to sacred temples across distant lands, or undertaking crucial assignments to secure the cult’s interests, these warriors are fueled by all-consuming love. They may be required to travel to Sparta or Argos or another city where Aphrodite Areia has a temple. Or the champion might be sent to any of the smaller shrines and temples to provide security, undergo an initiation, or assist in a special operation.

Promises

The following are the sacred promises made by a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior:

Shield the Beloved: Above all else, protect those who are dear to your heart. Be their unwavering shield against any threat, physical or emotional. No harm should befall them as long as you draw breath. Unleash your Heart’s Boundless Fury: Embrace the fire within you, the burning passion that fuels your actions. Unleash your righteous fury upon those who would harm your loved ones.
Vow Unbreakable Devotion: Pledge your loyalty and devotion to your chosen companions. Stand by their side in times of joy and hardship, offering support and guidance. Your oath is not limited to romantic love but extends to all forms of genuine connection.
Embrace Martial Excellence: Hone your combat skills to perfection, melding ferocity with strength. Let your blade strike true and your defense be impenetrable, for the safety of your loved ones relies on your skill and valor.

Hit Die: d10.

Requirements

To qualify to become a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior, a character must fulfill all the following criteria.

Base Attack Bonus: +3.
Skills: Intimidation 3 ranks, Knowledge (war) 3 ranks.
Alignment: Any chaotic.
Class Skills

The Champion of the Impassioned Warrior’s class skills are Craft (Int), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Knowledge (war) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the Champion of the Impassioned Warrior.

Impassioned (Ex)

At 1st level, an Impassioned Warrior can become impassioned as a swift action.

While impassioned, an impassioned warrior gains a +2 morale bonus to her Strength and Dexterity, as well as a +2 morale bonus on Will saves. An Impassioned Warrior can end this ability with a free action. An Impassioned Warrior can use this ability a number of rounds per day equal to 4 + her Impassioned Warrior level. At 4th, 7th, and 10th levels, the Impassioned Warrior gains 2 additional rounds in which she can be impassioned.

Warrior’s Ward (Su)

At 1st level, as an immediate action, an Impassioned Warrior can select one creature within 60 feet to be her ward for 1 minute or until the ward dies or the Impassioned Warrior chooses a different ward, whichever comes first. During this time, the ward gains a deflection bonus to its AC equal to the Impassioned Warrior’s Charisma modifier (minimum 1) and a number of temporary hit points equal to twice the Impassioned Warrior’s level. The Impassioned Warrior can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Charisma modifier (if positive). An Impassioned Warrior can only have one ward active at a time.

Spells. Beginning at 1st level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior gains the ability to cast a small number of divine spells which are drawn from the paladin spell list. A champion must choose and prepare her spells in advance.

To prepare or cast a spell, a champion must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a champion’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the champion’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a champion can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day.

Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table 3: Champion of the Impassioned Warrior. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells). When Table 3 indicates that the champion gets 0 spells per day of a given spell level, she gains only the bonus spells she would be entitled to based on her Charisma score for that spell level.

A champion must spend 1 hour each day in quiet prayer and meditation to regain her daily allotment of spells. A champion may prepare and cast any spell on the paladin spell list, provided that she can cast spells of that level, but she must choose which spells to prepare during her daily meditation.

Divine Grace (Su)

At 2nd level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior gains a bonus equal to her Charisma bonus (if any) on all Saving Throws.

Lay on Hands (Su)

Beginning at 2nd level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior can heal wounds (her own or those of others) by touch. Each day she can use this ability a number of times equal to 1/2 her champion level plus her Charisma modifier. With one use of this ability, a champion can heal 1d6 hit points of damage for every two champion levels she possesses. Using this ability is a standard action, unless the champion targets herself, in which case it is a swift action. Despite the name of this ability, a champion only needs one free hand to use this ability.

Alternatively, a champion can use this healing power to deal damage to undead creatures, dealing 1d6 points of damage for every two levels the champion possesses. Using lay on hands in this way requires a successful melee touch attack and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. Undead do not receive a saving throw against this damage.

Aura of Courage (Su)

At 3rd level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior is immune to fear (magical or otherwise). Each ally within 10 feet of her gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects. This ability functions only while the champion is conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead.

Divine Health (Ex)

At 3rd level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior is immune to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases, including mummy rot.

Mercy (Su)

At 3rd level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior can select one mercy. Each mercy adds an effect to the champion’s Lay on Hands ability. Whenever the champion uses Lay on Hands to heal damage to one target, the target also receives the additional effects from all of the mercies possessed by the champion. A mercy can remove a condition caused by a curse, disease, or poison without curing the affliction. Such conditions return after 1 hour unless the mercy actually removes the affliction that causes the condition.

The Champion of the Impassioned Warrior can select from the following mercies.

Dazed: The target is no longer dazed.
Deceived: The target can immediately attempt a new saving throw to disbelieve any ongoing illusions that it failed to disbelieve within the last minute.
Diseased: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as remove disease, using the champion’s level as the caster level.
Enfeebled: The champion dispels any magical effects that are reducing one of the target’s ability scores (champion’s choice).
Fatigued: The target is no longer fatigued.
Haunted: The champion’s Lay on Hands also acts as protection from evil, but only for the purpose of allowing a new saving throw against enchantment (charm) and enchantment (compulsion) effects, making the target immune to any attempts to possess or exercise mental control over the target, or preventing a life force from controlling the target (all as described in the second effect of protection from evil). Use the champion’s level as the caster level.
Riled: The champion’s Lay on Hands also acts as calm emotions, but only for the purpose of suppressing morale bonuses (such as from the rage spell) and emotion effects that aren’t fear effects. Use the champion’s level as the caster level.
Shaken: The target is no longer shaken.
Sickened: The target is no longer sickened.
Staggered: The target is no longer staggered, unless the target is at exactly 0 hit points.
Targeted: The champion’s Lay on Hands also acts as sanctuary, using the champion’s level as the caster level. The saving throw DC to negate this effect is equal to 10 + 1/2 the champion’s level + the champion’s Charisma modifier.
Instant Passion (Ex)

Upon reaching 4th level, the Impassioned Warrior can use her impassioned ability as a free action.

Divine Bond (Sp)

At 5th level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior forms a divine bond with Aphrodite Areia. This bond can take one of two forms. Once the form is chosen, it cannot be changed.

Bonded Weapon. The first type of bond allows the champion to enhance her weapon as a standard action by calling upon the aid of a daemonic spirit for 1 minute per champion level. When called, the spirit causes the weapon to shed light as a torch. At 1st level, this spirit grants the weapon a +1 enhancement bonus. For every three levels beyond 1st, the weapon gains another +1 enhancement bonus. These bonuses can be added to the weapon, stacking with existing weapon bonuses to a maximum of +5, or they can be used to add any of the following weapon properties: anarchic, brilliant energy, defending, disruption, flaming, flaming burst, keen, speed and stalking. Adding these properties consumes an amount of bonus equal to the property’s cost (see Table: Magic Weapon Special Abilities). These bonuses are added to any properties the weapon already has, but duplicate abilities do not stack. If the weapon is not magical, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before any other properties can be added. The bonus and properties granted by the spirit are determined when the spirit is called and cannot be changed until the spirit is called again. The daemonic spirit imparts no bonuses if the weapon is held by anyone other than the champion but resumes giving bonuses if returned to the champion. These bonuses apply to only one end of a double weapon. A champion can use this ability once per day at 1st level, and one additional time per day for every four levels beyond 1st.

If a weapon bonded with a daemonic spirit is destroyed, the champion loses the use of this ability for 30 days, or until she gains a level, whichever comes first. During this 30-day period, the champion takes a –1 penalty on attack and weapon damage rolls.

Bonded Mount. The second type of bond allows a champion to gain the service of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal steed to serve her in her crusades.

This mount is usually a heavy horse (for a Medium champion) or a pony (for a Small champion), although more exotic mounts, such as a boar, camel, or dog are also suitable. This mount functions as a druid’s animal companion, using the champion’s total character level as her effective druid level. Bonded mounts have an Intelligence of at least 6.

In addition to horses, a champion may select (at the GM’s discretion) some less ordinary creatures.

A Medium champion can select an elk, giant seahorse, giraffe, yak or zebra as a bonded mount.

A Small champion can select an antelope, capybara, eohippus, giant weasel, ram, reindeer, stag, or wolfdog as a bonded mount.

Upon reaching 6th level as a champion or 16th level in total character levels, whichever comes first, the champion can choose a flying horse, giant eagle, Pegasus, griffon, giant hawk, giant vulture, or giant owl as a bonded mount.

The auspice, bodyguard, racer, and totem guide archetypes are all particularly appropriate for a champion’s bonded mount.

Once per day, as a full-round action, a champion may magically call her mount to her side. This ability is the equivalent of a spell of a level equal to one third the champion’s level. The mount immediately appears adjacent to the champion. A champion can use this ability once per day at 5th level, and one additional time per day at 9th level.

Should the champion’s mount die, the champion may not summon another mount for 30 days or until she gains a champion or Heartfire Sentinel level, whichever comes first. During this 30-day period, the champion takes a –1 penalty on attack and weapon damage rolls.

Aura of Resolve (Su)

At 8th level, a Champion of the Impassioned Warrior is immune to charm spells and spell-like abilities. Each ally within 10 feet of her gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against charm effects. This ability functions only while the champion is conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead.
